newsitem.title: U S VIRGIN ISLANDS: U.S. Virgin Islands gives Westin 10-year tax break.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Virgin Islands gives Westin 10-year tax break.

text.p: Governor Roy Schneider has approved proposals for the Westin St.John Hotel Co to avoid paying most taxes for 10 years, as recommended by the Virgin Islands Industrial Development Commission.
The company, a subsidiary of Westin Hotels and Resorts, will invest $36 million to buy and refurbish the Great Cruz Bay Development Company, a Government House statement said on Thursday.

The tax breaks, the maximum allowed under the law, include 100 percent exemptions from real property taxes, gross receipts taxes and excise taxes on building materials. Others include a 90 percent exemption from income taxes and other breaks in customs duties.

Among the conditions Westin agreed to before the tax breaks were approved included employing at least 230 full-time workers, a work force comprised of at least 80 percent island residents, investment of at least $36 million, room discounts for Virgin Island residents during off-peak times, and funding of a $5,000 scholarship for a St.John student at the University of the Virgin Islands hospitality program.
The resort was formerly St.John's Hyatt Regency, which was closed by Hurricane Marilyn in 1995. Westin said it would open the resort betweeen October and December 1997.
